reason: I'd tap 'Hard to sleep' once or twice on the train home, but I already fall asleep to free rain sounds. Ten dollars a month on my budget is groceries.
objection: When I feel bad at night I don't want to write a sentence about it, I just want something to press play on.
would_change_my_mind: One-tap sessions that are clearly better than my free sleep sounds, at about $4 a month.

v1.why: A check-in form with a notes box the moment I sign in is exactly what I don't want at bedtime.

v2.why: The chips and skippable questions are easier, but I'd still drift back to my free sounds.

v3.why: Same as 2 for me; the journal and reports are more things asking me to write.

reason: An AI writing a script about my mental state and reading it to me in a fake voice is not something I'd let near my head. I'll stick with a podcast for the commute.
objection: It's an app built to ask how I feel every day and then generate something from it; that's the opposite of what I want.
would_change_my_mind: A therapist or real person I trust standing behind the scripts, and no daily questions.

v1.why: A daily check-in sheet plus a coin balance on every screen; that's two strikes.

v2.why: 'How do you feel now?' after every session is still the daily questioning I dislike.

v3.why: The 'Why?' on suggestions is the least bad, but it's still AI deciding things about my mood.

reason: I'd try it once after the kids are down because it's free, but YouTube already has hours of guided stuff I like. I've never paid for one of these and $10 won't be the first.
objection: An AI voice talking me through breathing feels a bit off, like it's pretending to know me.
would_change_my_mind: Hearing a sample that honestly sounds as warm as a real person, and staying free.

v1.why: Opening on someone else's chat about their REM sleep is the creepy feeling I was worried about.

v2.why: Cleaner and it's my own conversation, but YouTube is still free and good enough.

v3.why: Wearable and journal stuff isn't for me; nothing here beats free.

reason: I paid for Calm and stopped after a month, so I know how this goes for me. I'll use the free sessions and see if I'm still opening it in week three before I spend anything on $32k.
objection: Is a custom session actually better than a normal one, or is that the gimmick?
would_change_my_mind: If I'm still using the free tier after a month and can actually tell I sleep better, maybe the yearly plan, not monthly.

v1.why: Percentages like '24%, Needs improvement' feel made up and would make me trust it less.

v2.why: The chapter 2 tomorrow hook might get me back a few times, but that's what Calm's streaks did too.

v3.why: Progress in my own words is the first thing that might show me whether it's helping, so I'd keep the free tier.

reason: At bedtime I want sleep sounds, not a conversation. I'd tap a chip or two, but with the kids I'm out in ten minutes and a free sound app does that.
objection: Typing how I feel when I'm wiped out at night is the last thing I'll do.
would_change_my_mind: A ready-made sleep session I can start with one tap, that remembers what I liked without asking.

v1.why: Hamburger menu, check-in form, example chat; too many steps to get to the sound.

v2.why: Skippable onboarding is good, but it still wants a sentence before it plays anything.

v3.why: Same core loop as 2; the extras are nice to know about but I wouldn't use them.

reason: I already pay for one wellness app and use free sleep stories on top; I'd try this the night before a big deadline out of curiosity. Adding another $10 subscription isn't happening unless it replaces one.
objection: I already have this covered by apps and YouTube, so what does it do that they don't?
would_change_my_mind: A session built for the night before a specific meeting that clearly beats my current app, so I can cancel that one.

v1.why: Coins on every screen make it feel like a game, not something I'd pay for.

v2.why: Polished, but I'd use it twice and go back to my usual app.

v3.why: Best of the three and the 'Why?' is a nice touch, still not enough to switch.

reason: I'll download it the day I hear about it and show my friends the made-in-a-minute session. But on my budget I won't pay $10 for something that asks how I feel every single time.
objection: After every session it wants a mood answer; I'll get tired of being asked questions in a week.
would_change_my_mind: Making the check-ins optional and a cheaper tier around $5.

v1.why: The daily check-in pops up the moment I sign in; instant annoyance.

v2.why: Fun for the novelty, but 'How do you feel now?' every time wears thin.

v3.why: More things to fill in: a journal, reports from check-ins; it's question-heavy.

reason: I check my sleep score every morning, so I'll try it for a week and see if the number moves. I've never paid for one of these and it'd have to prove itself in the data first.
objection: Without seeing my sleep score improve, it's just another nice-sounding gimmick.
would_change_my_mind: Two weeks of my own wearable data showing better sleep on nights I used it.

v1.why: The progress numbers are clearly not mine, so they tell me nothing.

v2.why: Percentages still don't connect to my actual sleep tracker.

v3.why: Asking for my wearable is the only hook that could prove it works, if it actually reads my data.

reason: I'm on my phone at midnight anyway, so I'd try one instead of scrolling. But YouTube sleep videos are free and $10 a month is a lot on what I make.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube that do the job well enough.
would_change_my_mind: Seeing my Oura deep-sleep numbers go up on Aurelia nights, at a price nearer $5.

v1.why: Menu buried behind a button and a check-in form; I'd close it and open YouTube.

v2.why: I like seeing numbers on Progress, but they're not connected to my ring.

v3.why: Taking the numbers away and leaving the wearable off by default is the opposite of what I want.

reason: 'My mind keeps racing' is literally me most weeknights, and free YouTube stuff hasn't stopped the scrolling. If the first week's sessions actually get me off my phone, $10 is nothing next to being wrecked at work.
objection: I've got free sleep stuff already; this has to be clearly better or I'll cancel.

v1.why: Opening on someone else's conversation and a coin counter makes it feel like a demo, not mine.

v2.why: My own first session, a chapter waiting tomorrow; that gives me a reason to open it instead of scrolling.

v3.why: Same as 2 plus progress in words; I'd rather read that I'm sleeping better than see a percentage.
